key_insight: High-resolution hurricane LES shows that grid-dependent differences in mean wind and turbulence can materially change the aeroelastic loads seen by an idling wind turbine.
engineering_relevance: Accurate extreme-load design for turbines in tropical-cyclone regions requires high-fidelity inflow fields, not just coarse storm-scale wind estimates.
method: Large-eddy simulations of Hurricane Laura were run at three grid resolutions: 55.55 m, 25 m, and 10 m.
LES outputs were used directly as inflow for aeroelastic wind-turbine simulations.
The turbine response was evaluated as the hurricane passed a virtual turbine location.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports significant differences in mean wind and turbulent structures across the three LES resolutions, producing distinct turbine aeroelastic responses.
watch_item: Results are based on a virtual location and one storm case, so broader design guidance should be validated across more tracks, intensities, and turbine states.
paper_title: Hurricane Laura-induced loads on wind turbines -- Part I: High-fidelity modeling and sensitivity to turbulent inflow conditions
